item.text: I’m using SQLite through Node’s built-in database driver, which keeps the app lightweight and the data genuinely local—no external service or native addon required. The core catalog, cart totals, ranking, checkout, and creator metrics will all be SQL-backed; the React layer will consume those through Start server functions and API routes.

The product flow is now wired end-to-end: storefront filters call the catalog API, favorites and cart mutate SQLite, prompt pages load through server functions, checkout creates real order rows, and analytics reads SQL aggregates. I’m moving into the visual pass now—matching the source’s spacing, overlays, irregular masonry proportions, desktop sidebar, and compact mobile dock before running builds.
